name: [Portal] Restricted Markdown for medailonek text (BE)
description:
### Summary

This task delivers a shared server-side component that safely renders the text partners write for their medailonek, the public profile card shown on partneri.shoptet.cz and doplnky.shoptet.cz. In the new Partner Portal, agencies, freelancers, affiliate partners and addon developers will write this text themselves instead of Shoptet staff editing WordPress by hand, so unrestricted formatting could break the layout of the public sites or introduce unsafe content. The task defines and documents a restricted subset of Markdown, implements one converter that turns stored text into safe HTML with raw HTML and images stripped and links limited to http and https, adds a reusable validation rule that reports length and disallowed constructs per field, and derives plain text for snippets and meta fallbacks. The same converter must produce identical output wherever it is used: the portal editing preview, the publication review in CRM and the future public API. Building any screen, storing the text or deciding the publication process is out of scope; those tasks consume this component.

### Why?

Partners will write their medailonek text themselves. Today that text lives as free WordPress content on the partner websites; the MVP scope requires a restricted Markdown so partners cannot break the layout of partneri.shoptet.cz or doplnky.shoptet.cz. The same rendering is needed in three places (portal edit preview, publication review, public read API), so it has to be one shared server-side component, not per-screen logic.

### What?

Decide and document the allowed Markdown subset for medailonek text fields (description, benefit, priceText; metaDescription stays plain text) and implement one server-side converter that turns stored Markdown into safe HTML. Raw HTML and disallowed syntax are stripped, links limited to http(s), output deterministic. Includes a validation rule reusable by the edit form (max length, disallowed constructs reported per field) and a plain-text derivation for snippets and meta fallbacks.

### Acceptance Criteria

Allowed subset is documented in the package README; raw HTML and embedded images are rejected, links only http(s)

One service converts Markdown → HTML; identical input gives identical output on every call site

Validator rejects text over the configured length and reports disallowed constructs with a field-level message

Plain-text derivation (metaDescription fallback, list snippets) comes from the same service

Unit tests cover every allowed construct, every rejected construct, XSS payloads (script tags, 

javascript:

 links, event attributes) and CZ/SK/HU diacritics

Contract test: rendered HTML of a sample profile is byte-identical on the portal preview path and the public API path

New code passes PHPStan level 10

### Open questions

- Portal edit preview: render server-side through this service (one renderer, no new JS dependency) or add a Markdown library to `admin/react`? Decision affects the edit-screen task.

### Technical notes

_Generated by Claude Fable 5.1, 2026-09-16_

- `league/commonmark ^2.10` is already a dependency (`composer.json:123`). Safe config already in use: `crm/admin/controllers/AdminTooling/SqlConsoleDetailController.php:41` (`GithubFlavoredMarkdownConverter`, `html_input=strip`, `allow_unsafe_links=false`); copy it and trim extensions to the allowed subset.
- No Markdown renderer or HTML sanitizer exists in JS (`admin/react/package.json`, `design-system/`); server-side rendering avoids a new dependency.
- Closest existing sanitizer for user/AI text: `cms/packages/AiRnd/Html/AiHtmlSanitizer.php` (reference only, different purpose).
- Storage: `partner_lng.description / benefit / priceText` (`database/schema/st_crm.sql` L2533).
- Today's public consumer reads `services_lng.expert*` raw in `marketplace/app/Addon/Helper.php:64`; the public API task should route through this converter instead.
